newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady vs dlr in spot, forwards.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady vs dlr in spot, forwards.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.60/61 per dollar on Thursday, unchanged from the opening rates dealers said.
The market was stuck to a narrow range throughout the day.

"The RBI (Reserve Bank of India) tried to buy - but I don't think they did as the market closed early because of cyclone rumours," said a dealer. The RBI has been buying dollars regularly in recent months to arrest the rupee's rise.
The rupee continued to gain in the forward dollar market on Thursday but the appearance of some payers (of premia) toward the close led to a mild correction, dealers said.
"This (current premia in the forward dollar market) makes sense (for importers to cover forwards)," R.K.Das, chief of forex and treasury at export firm Adani Exports Ltd said.
He said he did not expect the rupee to strengthen further on the forward market.

Das told Reuters his firm followed a strategy of covering 50 percent of forward dollar requirements. He said it would be a good strategy for exporters to buy forwards for the short term and sell their forward receivables long.
